questions.scenario: Your friend falls down while playing gully cricket and is bleeding from the knee. What do you do?

options.text: I quickly grab water, wash the wound, and apply a tight bandage with my own hands.
I check if they can bend their knee to ensure there is no internal bone fracture.
I apply Dettol and a band-aid very neatly so it doesn't leave a bad scar later.
I shout for help, tell someone to get the first-aid box, and arrange an auto to go home.

questions.scenario: In the Biology lab, the teacher shows a real heart or kidney specimen. What is your reaction?

options.text: I want to put on gloves and physically touch or dissect it.
I carefully observe the veins and try to understand how the blood flows logically.
I am fascinated by how beautifully complex and structured the human body looks.
I stand back and make sure everyone gets a chance to see without crowding the table.

questions.scenario: When you watch medical dramas (like Sanjivani, Grey's Anatomy, or Good Doctor), what excites you?

options.text: The intense emergency room scenes where doctors are literally saving a dying patient.
The puzzle-solving part where they figure out a mysterious rare disease.
The scenes where a patient's face or body is beautifully reconstructed after a fire.
The politics and management of running the massive hospital.

questions.scenario: Someone in your house gets a high fever and stomach ache at 2 AM.

options.text: I stay awake, physically putting cold wet cloth on their forehead to bring the fever down.
I Google their exact symptoms to figure out if it's food poisoning or a viral infection.
I try to make them feel comfortable by adjusting the pillows and keeping the room dim.
I quickly find the emergency doctor's number and organize the medical file.

questions.scenario: You have to do a massive 500-piece jigsaw puzzle.

options.text: I aggressively sit on the floor and start joining pieces by trial and error.
I analyze the picture on the box first and group pieces by their logical patterns.
I focus on the corner pieces and the beautiful color gradients first.
I divide the pieces among my siblings and tell everyone which section to solve.

questions.scenario: If you had a 'doctor' superpower, what would it be?

options.text: Healing physical wounds and fixing broken bones instantly with my hands.
Looking at someone and instantly knowing what disease they have.
Removing all scars and physical flaws to make people look perfect.
Curing 1,000 people at once by organizing a massive free medical camp.

questions.scenario: Your computer or bicycle breaks down.

options.text: I open it up with tools and forcefully try to fix the mechanical parts.
I do a step-by-step check to diagnose exactly which wire or software is failing.
I fix it and then paint or polish it so it looks brand new.
I calculate if repairing it is worth the money or if I should just buy a new one.

questions.scenario: You visit a massive hospital in your city to meet a relative.

options.text: I peek into the operation theatre (OT) doors wishing I could see a surgery.
I look at the MRI and X-Ray reports hanging near the bed trying to read them.
I notice the lighting and how clean the hospital looks.
I look at the huge crowd and wonder how the hospital manages so many patients daily.

questions.scenario: Every medical job has stress. What stress can you handle best?

options.text: Standing for 10 hours straight doing physical work with no sleep.
Reading 50 boring medical textbooks to find the cure for one patient.
Doing highly delicate, tiny stitch work that takes extreme patience.
Dealing with angry relatives and managing a strict budget.

questions.scenario: How do you want your future patients to describe you?

options.text: 'He/She saved my life in the emergency room!'
'He/She was the only doctor smart enough to figure out my disease.'
'He/She completely restored my confidence and my smile.'
'He/She runs the best, most organized hospital in the city.'

Trauma_Surgeon.title: Surgeon / Emergency Doctor
Trauma_Surgeon.primary_match_text: You are brave, action-oriented, and not easily grossed out! You love fixing things with your hands and thrive in high-pressure situations.
Trauma_Surgeon.day_in_the_life: Standing in the Operation Theatre, performing life-saving surgeries, and fixing physical injuries in the ER.
Trauma_Surgeon.alternative_match_text: Your strong stomach and quick hands also make you a great fit for Orthopedics (Bone Doctor) or the Armed Forces Medical Corps.
Trauma_Surgeon.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Clear NEET to pursue MBBS, followed by an MS in General Surgery.

Diagnostician_MD.title: MD Physician / Diagnostician
Diagnostician_MD.primary_match_text: You are the medical detective! You have a highly analytical brain that loves connecting symptoms, reading reports, and solving health puzzles.
Diagnostician_MD.day_in_the_life: Checking patients, analyzing complex blood reports, and prescribing the exact treatment to cure rare diseases.
Diagnostician_MD.alternative_match_text: Your puzzle-solving brain makes you a perfect fit for Pathology (Lab Doctor), Neurology, or Medical Research.
Diagnostician_MD.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Clear NEET to pursue MBBS, followed by an MD in General Medicine.

Plastic_Surgeon.title: Plastic & Reconstructive Surgeon
Plastic_Surgeon.primary_match_text: You perfectly combine medicine with art. You have a creative eye for detail, aesthetics, and extreme patience for delicate work.
Plastic_Surgeon.day_in_the_life: Performing surgeries to reconstruct faces after accidents or doing aesthetic procedures to boost people's confidence.
Plastic_Surgeon.alternative_match_text: If you want a creative medical field, you would also excel in Dermatology (Skin Specialist) or Cosmetology.
Plastic_Surgeon.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Clear NEET for MBBS, do MS in Surgery, then M.Ch in Plastic Surgery.

Hospital_Administrator.title: Hospital Administrator / Chief Medical Officer
Hospital_Administrator.primary_match_text: You are a born leader. You understand healthcare, but you prefer managing the entire system, leading doctors, and running the business.
Hospital_Administrator.day_in_the_life: Managing a 500-bed hospital, ensuring oxygen/medicines are always available, and expanding the hospital's branches.
Hospital_Administrator.alternative_match_text: With your commanding nature, you can also build a massive Healthcare Tech Startup or excel in Public Health Policy.
Hospital_Administrator.roadmap: Take PCB or Commerce in 11th/12th. You can do BBA/B.Sc/MBBS followed by an MBA in Hospital & Healthcare Management.
